lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: Small Claims of the Multiverse. One hundred and ten point two. All rise.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: This is Small Claims of the Multiverse. I am Judge Alvarez-Penhallow. Please be seated, in whatever way you sit.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: Small Claims of the Multiverse. Disputes between dimensions, settled with dignity, and a gavel.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Small Claims of the Multiverse. No claim too small. Several, frankly, far too small. We hear them anyway.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: You are listening to Courtroom Four, on one one oh point two. The court is in session. The court is always in session.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: Case four thousand and six. The Upper Atmosphere of Vell, against the Lower Atmosphere of Vell. A cloud, parked across both, for nine days.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: The Echo of Hollow Point, against the Original Shout. A claim for unpaid royalties, going back eleven centuries.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Proceed. Proceed. Proceed.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: Dimension Nine, against Dimension Nine B. A garden fence, eleven inches over the boundary, in a direction neither party can point to.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: Mister Barnaby Chell, a ghost, against the tenants of number four, Lantern Row. A noise complaint. The tenants are too quiet. He finds it unsettling.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: The Tuesday of the Grey Reach, against the Wednesday of the Grey Reach. Three hours, borrowed in good faith, never returned.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: A single sock, left foot, against a washing machine in the Overlap. Wrongful relocation. The sock seeks the return of its partner.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: The Tide of Pellam, against the Moon of Pellam. The tide says it is being pulled about. The moon says it never laid a finger on it.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: Mister Gideon Fairweather, against Mister Gideon Fairweather, of next Thursday. Reimbursement for a haircut the plaintiff hasn't had yet, and will regret.

clips.title: The Snow Globe and the Shelf

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: The residents of a snow globe, against the shelf it stands on. A shaking incident, during a door being slammed, on the evening of the fourth.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: The Marrowgate Lending Library, against a small dragon. A book of poems, returned slightly toasted. The dragon counterclaims that the poems were very exciting.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: A lighthouse, retired, against a fog bank. The lighthouse alleges it has been followed, every evening, for forty years.

lines.speaker: The Plaintiff
lines.text: Your Honour, I have never been so inconvenienced in all my dimensions. And I have a great many dimensions.

lines.speaker: The Plaintiff
lines.text: I want it noted that I was there first. I was there first in every version of events. I have the versions here, in a folder.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: The court will take the folder. The court notes the folder is also a dimension. Please don't put it down near the others.

lines.speaker: The Defendant
lines.text: In my defence, Your Honour, it was like that when I found it.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: When did you find it?

lines.speaker: The Defendant
lines.text: Just after I did it.

lines.speaker: Ms. Castellane, for the Defence
lines.text: My client would like a moment, Your Honour.

lines.speaker: Ms. Castellane, for the Defence
lines.text: Objection, Your Honour. Counsel is leading the witness.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Leading them where?

lines.speaker: Ms. Castellane, for the Defence
lines.text: Somewhere nicer, Your Honour. There's a view.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Overruled. Everyone deserves a view. Carry on, Mister Lusk, but come straight back.

lines.speaker: Mr. Lusk, for the Plaintiff
lines.text: I call an expert witness. A professor of comparative ownership.

lines.speaker: An Expert Witness
lines.text: Your Honour, in my professional opinion, the item in question belongs to whoever is holding it, unless somebody else is also holding it, in which case it belongs to the situation.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: And who owns the situation?

lines.speaker: An Expert Witness
lines.text: Nobody, Your Honour. That's why we're all here.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Have the two parties tried simply talking to one another?

lines.speaker: The Plaintiff
lines.text: We tried, Your Honour. We're from different dimensions. Every time we talk, one of us is yesterday.

lines.speaker: The Defendant
lines.text: It's usually me.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Let the record show the court sympathises. The court has been yesterday too. It doesn't suit everybody.

lines.speaker: Mr. Lusk, for the Plaintiff
lines.text: I'd like to enter exhibit A, Your Honour.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: Exhibit A. A cardboard box. Inside the box, a second, smaller box. Inside that, a note, which reads, nearly.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Nearly what?

lines.speaker: Mr. Lusk, for the Plaintiff
lines.text: That's rather the point of the case, Your Honour.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Order. Order. Bailiff, the cloud in the public gallery is raining again.

lines.speaker: Bailiff Mutch
lines.text: Shall I remove it, Your Honour?

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: No. Give it a tissue. It's been a very emotional morning for everyone.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Is the defendant present?

lines.speaker: Ms. Castellane, for the Defence
lines.text: Partly, Your Honour.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Which part?

lines.speaker: Ms. Castellane, for the Defence
lines.text: The part that's sorry, Your Honour. The rest of my client sends its apologies, but it's in another dimension, and it isn't sorry at all.

lines.speaker: A Dimension
lines.text: Your Honour. I wish to give evidence.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: The court recognises the dimension. Please keep your voice down. You're rattling the windows in two other courtrooms.

lines.speaker: A Dimension
lines.text: Sorry. I only wished to say that I saw everything.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Everything?

lines.speaker: A Dimension
lines.text: I'm a dimension, Your Honour. I can't help it. It's all just there.

lines.speaker: A Very Small Party
lines.text: Your Honour! Down here! I'd like to be heard!

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Bailiff, would you lift the very small party onto the witness stand, please. Gently.

lines.speaker: Bailiff Mutch
lines.text: Up you come.

lines.speaker: A Very Small Party
lines.text: Thank you. I just want to say that this whole business has been very big, from where I'm standing.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Noted. It has been very big from up here too.

lines.speaker: The Plaintiff
lines.text: I'd like to call a witness from next week, Your Honour.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: The court allows it. Where is the witness?

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: They'll be here next week, Your Honour.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Then we shall hear their evidence next week, and pretend, for now, that we have. Everyone look convinced.

lines.speaker: Ms. Castellane, for the Defence
lines.text: Your Honour, my client did not take the item. My client was merely standing very close to the item when it left.

lines.speaker: Mr. Lusk, for the Plaintiff
lines.text: Your Honour, the item was in the defendant's coat.

lines.speaker: Ms. Castellane, for the Defence
lines.text: A coincidence. My client has a very large coat. Things get into it.

lines.speaker: Mr. Lusk, for the Plaintiff
lines.text: Objection, Your Honour. Relevance.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: To what?

lines.speaker: Mr. Lusk, for the Plaintiff
lines.text: To anything, Your Honour. Anything at all.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Sustained. The court has been wondering about that for some years.

lines.speaker: The Defendant
lines.text: I'd like to say something, Your Honour. In all the dimensions I've lived in, this is the only one where anybody has ever taken me to court.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: And how does that feel?

lines.speaker: The Defendant
lines.text: Honestly? Quite flattering. It's nice to be noticed.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Clerk Odell, would you read back the plaintiff's last statement?

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: The plaintiff said, and I quote: it's the principle of the thing, and also the thing.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Thank you. The court has rarely heard it put so clearly.

lines.speaker: Ms. Castellane, for the Defence
lines.text: Your Honour, my client has prepared a statement.

lines.speaker: The Defendant
lines.text: I am sorry for any inconvenience that may or may not have occurred, in any timeline where it may or may not have occurred, to anybody who was there, or who wasn't, but heard.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: That is the most thorough apology the court has received. The court is going to frame it.

lines.speaker: Mr. Lusk, for the Plaintiff
lines.text: Your Honour, I direct the court's attention to the plaintiff's face. Look at it. That is the face of someone who has been wronged.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: The court has looked. The court notes the plaintiff's face has been like that since the plaintiff arrived. And in the corridor. And in the photograph on the claim form.

lines.speaker: Mr. Lusk, for the Plaintiff
lines.text: Wronged for a long time, Your Honour.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Before we go further, does anybody in this courtroom have any idea what this case is actually about?

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: The clerk does, Your Honour. Roughly. In outline.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Splendid. Then we have a quorum.

lines.speaker: Bailiff Mutch
lines.text: Your Honour, there's a goose in the corridor asking whether it's needed.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Tell the goose it isn't a suspect here. This isn't that sort of station.

lines.speaker: Bailiff Mutch
lines.text: It says it'll wait. Just in case.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: The court finds that everybody is a little bit right, which is the most annoying verdict available. Costs shared. Next.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Case dismissed. Both parties are to shake hands, using whatever they have.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Judgment for the plaintiff in this dimension, and for the defendant in all the others. Please sort it out amongst yourselves, in the car park.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: The court awards damages of one sincere apology, payable now.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: That will do. Case closed.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Settled out of court, apparently, while I was talking. Well done, both of you. Odell, the next one.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Adjourned until the matter makes sense. Odell, mark it as a long adjournment.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: The longest, Your Honour.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: The court rules for the defendant, but would like it known that it didn't enjoy doing so, and it won't be doing it again.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: The item is to be returned to whoever misses it most.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: That's both of you. Then share it. On alternate Tuesdays.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Judgment reserved. I'll reserve it somewhere nice, with a view, and come back for it after lunch.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: The court finds for the plaintiff. The defendant will pay costs of one hour of sitting quietly, thinking about it.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: No case to answer. There's barely a case to ask. Off you go, the lot of you. Mind the cloud.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: The court is in recess. Please remain seated, or, if you have no means of sitting, remain whatever you are.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: The tea trolley is in the corridor. Parties from opposing dimensions are asked to take turns.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: We'll take a short recess. Fifteen minutes, local time. If you don't have local time, borrow some from the clerk.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: I have plenty, Your Honour. It's in the drawer.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: Court notices. Witnesses who exist only in the past tense are asked to give evidence before lunch, while they still can.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: Lost property, at the clerk's desk: one umbrella, one shadow, one very small hat. The hat was fined for contempt, and has paid.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: Today's docket, Your Honour. Forty one cases. Six fences. Three hours, borrowed. Two moons. One hat.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Just the one hat?

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: It's a very serious hat, Your Honour.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: I'm often asked why I take claims from the weather. The answer is simple. Everybody complains about the weather. Nobody asks what the weather thinks.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: It has a great deal to say. It says most of it on Tuesdays.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: People ask me why Clerk Odell reads the cases in that voice.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: Which voice, Your Honour?

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: That one, Odell. Like a forecast for a sea that isn't there.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: Moderate, Your Honour. Becoming good.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: The court notes that a relay ship has drifted into its jurisdiction. Good evening, operator.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: You've done nothing wrong. Drifting is not an offence. Not knowing why you are drifting is not an offence either. It's merely interesting.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: I take my notes in green ink. Red ink is for mistakes. Black ink is for the record. Green ink is for things I found delightful.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: My notebooks are almost entirely green. Clerk Odell says it's unprofessional. Clerk Odell has a green pen too. I've seen it.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: Small Claims of the Multiverse is supported by Fenwright and Daughters, interdimensional notaries.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: Witnessing signatures in every dimension since the first contract, which was between a cliff and the sea, and is still being argued about.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: Fenwright and Daughters. We'll stamp anything. Within reason. Reason is extra.

lines.speaker: Mr. Lusk, for the Plaintiff
lines.text: Long day in court? Throat raw from objecting? Try Plaintiff's Pastilles.

lines.speaker: Mr. Lusk, for the Plaintiff
lines.text: Honey, lemon, and a faint taste of justice. Suitable for counsel, witnesses and the occasional dimension.

lines.speaker: Ms. Castellane, for the Defence
lines.text: Defendants may experience the same benefits. It's only fair.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: This court is not permitted to endorse products. However.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Grumbel's Ladders have appeared before this bench forty one times, as plaintiff, defendant and witness, and have never once been found to be anything other than a ladder.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: That is more than can be said for most of us. Up is a choice.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: All rise for Petty Sessions. Judge Alvarez-Penhallow presiding. Fences first, then clouds.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Good morning. Before we start, a reminder that the court does not accept evidence in the form of a hunch, a vibe, or a strong feeling about a neighbour.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Unless the neighbour is the weather, in which case, we'll allow it.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: The court is now sitting for the Late List. Parties who only exist after dark, please come forward. Mind the step. It's darker than it looks.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: The Late List. Tonight, eleven noise complaints from the void. The void says everything else is too loud.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: It has a point. It always has a point. It's a very small point, in a very large silence.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: Your Honour, the plaintiff in the next case is a shadow, who says it's been walked out on.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Not Greg?

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: No, Your Honour. The other way round. Its person left it.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Oh. Oh, that's much worse. Bring it some tea. Bring it a chair it can lie across.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: It's Friday, and this is Landmark Rulings. The great precedents of the Tribunal, revisited from the bench.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Landmark ruling number one. The Sea, against the Shore. The oldest case on our books.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: The Sea claimed the beach. The Shore claimed the beach. The beach declined to give evidence, and simply lay there.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Counsel for the Sea argued that the beach was wet, and wet things are the Sea's. Counsel for the Shore argued that the beach was sandy, and sandy things are the Shore's.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: The court ruled that the wet bit belongs to the Sea, and the dry bit belongs to the Shore, and the bit in between belongs to whoever is standing on it at the time, eating an ice cream.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: The ruling stands to this day, Your Honour. Twice a day, it's tested.

clips.title: In the Matter of the Last Biscuit

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Landmark ruling number two. In the matter of the last biscuit.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: Eleven parties, Your Honour, from four dimensions, all of whom had been offered the last biscuit, and all of whom had said, oh, no, you have it.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: The biscuit sat on the plate for nine years. It became a landmark in its own right. People came to see it.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: The court ruled that the last biscuit belongs to whoever did not ask for it. Since nobody had, it belonged to everybody, and was broken into eleven pieces, by the Bailiff, very carefully.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: Mutch still talks about it, Your Honour.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: So do I, Odell. So do I.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Landmark ruling number three. Tuesday, against Tuesday.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: A week in the Grey Reach was found to contain two Tuesdays. Each claimed to be the real one. Each had its own weather, its own bin day, and its own very strong opinion.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: The week asked the court to choose. The court declined. You cannot ask a week to choose between its days. It's cruel. And the days can hear you.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: The court ruled that the week may keep both Tuesdays, on condition that it treat them equally, and that Wednesday be told gently.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: Wednesday took it very well, Your Honour. All things considered.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: Your Honour, eleven planets have filed claims for the same missing moon.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Then the moon is ordered to appear before this court. Immediately. Or, failing that, tonight, where people can see it.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Order. Order. The court is aware that everything smells of toast.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: The court did not make the toast. The court would like that on the record, and also, if possible, some toast.

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: Your Honour, the whole gallery is humming the same song.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: So is the bench, Odell. Nobody can finish it. Adjourned until somebody remembers how it goes.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: That wasn't the gavel. Somebody knocked. Three times.

lines.speaker: Bailiff Mutch
lines.text: Nobody at the door, Your Honour.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Then let the record show the court was knocked on, by nobody. We'll hear them when they're ready.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: The sky outside the windows is a colour the court has no word for.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Clerk Odell, enter it in the record as, indescribable, and underline it twice. In green ink.

lines.speaker: Bailiff Mutch
lines.text: Your Honour, there's a pigeon on the witness stand.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: It seems to know me. Has it been sworn in?

lines.speaker: Bailiff Mutch
lines.text: It's nodding, Your Honour.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Good enough. Go on, then. Tell us everything.

clips.title: The Haunted House against Its Ghost

lines.speaker: Clerk Odell
lines.text: A special Halloween hearing. Number nine, Crowsfoot Lane, a house, against its ghost. The house claims the ghost hasn't haunted it properly in years.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: Is this true?

lines.speaker: Ms. Castellane, for the Defence
lines.text: My client has been very tired, Your Honour. Two hundred years of rattling. It's taken up knitting.

lines.speaker: Judge Alvarez-Penhallow
lines.text: The court orders one proper haunting, on the thirty first, with chains, and the knitting may come along. Case closed. Boo.
